newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's CTC says costs have fallen.
newsitem.headline: Chile's CTC says costs have fallen.

text.p: Chile's largest telephone company Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile SA (CTC) said it has achieved an important reduction in consolidated operating costs in 1995 and 1996.

"This (cost saving) policy has borne fruit which has meant an important reduction in consolidated operational costs as is shown by the results in our accounts for the year ending 31 December 1995 and in the first half of 1996," said the company in a statement.
CTC's shares opened lower in Santiago and New York on news of a letter from general manager Jacinto Diaz to workers in which he warned costs were growing faster than revenues.
The company's shares were trading mid-morning down 0.21 percent at 2,325 pesos, while its American Depositary Receipts were off 0.9 percent at 96-1/2.
CTC said in the statement that it has been putting special emphasis on reducing costs since 1995.
"Concern about costs and expenses in operations and investment projects is an issue which is regularly evaluated in all instances by the company," it said.

In his letter, sent to employees on August 27 but published Friday, Diaz said a cost control campaign in the first half 1996 failed to bring the desired results, especially in the area of payments for good and services.
If the company does not succeed in tightening cost controls, then the situation "will affect all of us working at CTC," said Diaz.

CTC reported operating income of 54.1 billion pesos for the first half of 1996 on revenues of 180.8 billion pesos, against operating income of 46.3 billion pesos on revenues of 158 billion pesos in the same period 1995.
The firm, which operates local, long-distance and mobile telephone services, is 43-percent owned by Telefonica de Espana .
